chapters.title: Chapter 1 — Double letters
chapters.description: Words ending in a double f, l, s or z, or in ck, plus five of the Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: A little word we put before a thing, as in "the cat".
meaning.example: We looked up and saw the moon.

meaning.definition: A little word we put before one thing, as in "a cat".
meaning.example: Mum gave me a red apple.

meaning.definition: The word you use to talk about yourself.
meaning.example: I can ride my bike.

meaning.definition: A little word that links a thing to what it looks or acts like.
meaning.example: The sky is blue today.

meaning.definition: Belonging to a boy or a man.
meaning.example: The boy put on his coat.

meaning.definition: A small gust of air, wind or smoke.
meaning.example: The wind gave a puff and the leaves moved.

meaning.definition: A metal cup that makes a ringing sound when it is hit.
meaning.example: The school bell rings at nine.

meaning.definition: A gentle touch on the cheek with your lips.
meaning.example: Gran gave me a kiss goodnight.

meaning.definition: The humming sound a bee makes.
meaning.example: I heard a buzz by the flowers.

meaning.definition: A bird with a flat beak that swims on water.
meaning.example: A duck swam across the pond.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 — Words ending nk
chapters.description: Words that end in nk, plus five Year 1 common exception words that end in the long e sound.

meaning.definition: A word for a boy or a man you are talking about.
meaning.example: He can run very fast.

meaning.definition: The word you use for yourself, as in "give it to me".
meaning.example: Please give the ball to me.

meaning.definition: A word for a girl or a woman you are talking about.
meaning.example: She likes to paint pictures.

meaning.definition: The word for yourself and other people together.
meaning.example: We play in the park.

meaning.definition: A word for what you are, or what you hope to turn into.
meaning.example: I want to be a doctor.

meaning.definition: A place where people keep and borrow money.
meaning.example: Dad went to the bank at lunch.

meaning.definition: A pale red colour, like a flamingo.
meaning.example: She wore a pink hat.

meaning.definition: To take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
meaning.example: I like to drink cold water.

meaning.definition: To tell someone you are glad for what they did.
meaning.example: Please thank Gran for the lovely card.

meaning.definition: The long nose of an elephant, or the thick stem of a tree.
meaning.example: The elephant lifted a log with its trunk.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 — Words ending tch
chapters.description: Words that end in tch after a short vowel, plus five Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: A word that shows who owns or holds something.
meaning.example: My sister has a new bag.

meaning.definition: The word we use instead of "is" when we talk about the past.
meaning.example: It was sunny all day.

meaning.definition: A little word that joins two things, as in "a cup of tea".
meaning.example: I drank a cup of milk.

meaning.definition: A little word that shows where someone is going.
meaning.example: We walk to the shop.

meaning.definition: To carry out an action or a job.
meaning.example: I will do my homework now.

meaning.definition: To grab something that is thrown or falling.
meaning.example: Can you catch the ball?

meaning.definition: A game between two teams.
meaning.example: We won the football match.

meaning.definition: A piece of cloth sewn over a hole.
meaning.example: Mum sewed a patch on my jeans.

meaning.definition: To go and bring something back.
meaning.example: Please fetch my bag from the car.

meaning.definition: One loop of thread made with a needle.
meaning.example: She sewed one more stitch in the cloth.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 — The v sound at the end
chapters.description: English words do not end in v, so a silent e follows it: five Year 1 exception words and five that show the rule.

meaning.definition: To like someone or something very much.
meaning.example: I love my little brother.

meaning.definition: To move towards a person or place.
meaning.example: Please come and sit by me.

meaning.definition: A few, or a part of something.
meaning.example: May I have some grapes?

meaning.definition: The number 1.
meaning.example: I have one sister.

meaning.definition: One time only.
meaning.example: We went to the sea once.

meaning.definition: To own or hold something.
meaning.example: We have a cat at home.

meaning.definition: To hand something to someone.
meaning.example: Please give me a turn on the swing.

meaning.definition: The number 5.
meaning.example: A hand has five fingers.

meaning.definition: A warm cover for your hand with places for your fingers.
meaning.example: Put a glove on each hand.

meaning.definition: To jump into water head first.
meaning.example: She can dive into the pool.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 — Adding s and es
chapters.description: Plural words made by adding s or es to the end, plus five Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: The word for the person you are talking to.
meaning.example: I can see you over there.

meaning.definition: Belonging to the person you are talking to.
meaning.example: Is this your pencil?

meaning.definition: The word for other people or things together.
meaning.example: They are playing in the garden.

meaning.definition: The word that goes with "you", "we" and "they" instead of "is".
meaning.example: We are at home.

meaning.definition: The word we use instead of "are" when we talk about the past.
meaning.example: The birds were singing this morning.

meaning.definition: More than one dog.
meaning.example: Two dogs ran along the beach.

meaning.definition: More than one hen, which is a farm bird.
meaning.example: The hens lay eggs on the farm.

meaning.definition: More than one box.
meaning.example: We packed the toys in three boxes.

meaning.definition: The plates and bowls we eat from.
meaning.example: Dad washed the dishes after tea.

meaning.definition: More than one fox, a wild animal with a bushy tail.
meaning.example: Two foxes ran across the field.
